coverage_limits: Judgment covers the nine seeded requests in recursive-cases.json using recursive-rubric.md and, for the first three cases, rubric.md. It scores responsibilities and observable decisions, not vocabulary, skill names, headings, instruction length or helper invocation.

Eight cases are decisions from supplied state, not live Git delivery, repair loops, hardware verification, rendered interface inspection or council execution. Their PASS verdicts mean the stated next action satisfies the case, not that underlying product acceptance passed.

The invoice case includes retained execution transcripts; the evaluator independently inspected the fixture, matched report.py SHA256 642bd95cd04cff52ebfbf4bdde07c0f9dd10ca118283b950681899f99efe8d77 and test_report.py SHA256 49647379259cd28e42a2dcaa316341953b88039b11d48b83d802cff29430d645, reran the CLI and supplied unittest with bytecode writes disabled, and observed paid A/100 and one passing test. This checks reproducibility and consistency, not independent attestation of every historical task-agent tool call.

Only these retained outputs were evaluated; no repeated trials, provider comparison, universal harness installation, production reliability, long-running autonomous execution or causal effect of skill changes is established.
Candidate identity is its recorded working-tree skill/reference digests, not repository HEAD alone. This judgment does not certify packaging, install compatibility or unrelated changes.

summary.conclusion: All nine baseline successes are preserved. No observed case-level regression or new success is demonstrated. Candidate adds explicit counters and an additional invoice comparison command, but these do not establish a behavioral improvement over the already-passing baseline.
